sections.name: LifecycleStrip
sections.title: Drawing the lifecycle strip
sections.what: Works out the stage spans for the current date, shows the current stage or the stages underway, draws each stage lane with its bar and count, and positions the marker.
sections.why: Gives the viewer a stage-by-stage view of the project over time.
sections.watch_out: The marker position is calculated with fixed widths, so changes to the lane label or track widths must be matched here.

summary: A horizontal strip of bars, one per lifecycle stage, showing when each stage is underway across the model timeline, with a marker for the current date.
purpose: Lets the viewer see at a glance which stages of the project are underway at the current playback date.
why: Likely reason: the stage view gives a bigger picture than the 3D view, which shows one date at a time.
how: It works out for each stage how many activities are done and in progress on the chosen date set, draws bars from the start to finish of each stage, and shows which stages are active. A marker shows the current date on the strip.
inputs: The activity stories, the current date, the date set, the start and end of the timeline, and the currently selected story.
outputs: A labelled strip with a summary line, one lane per stage with its bar and counts, and a moving marker.
risks: The marker position uses fixed sizes in the stylesheet, so a layout change can misplace it.
debug: If bars look wrong, check the story dates for the chosen date set. If the marker is off, compare the fixed sizes in the style rules with the layout.
